title: yadgar/task-db
$comment:
CLOSURE IS PER CHART (ADR-0850): this schema closes only what task-db owns — its own root and every block below. It does not speak for the parent chart, the platform chart, or any other module.

CLOSED (own): image, database (+instance, +instance.storage, +instance.tls, +mariadbOperator), tls, autoscaling (+kedaOperator), topologySpread, networkPolicy (+scrapeFrom). A typo inside any of these, or at the root, is refused at render, naming the key and its JSON path (ledger 990, ADR-0847).

OPEN (bare {}, any subkey passes): `global` — read by no template in this chart, but forwarded by the parent's coalesced values to every child, so closing it here would refuse the parent's own default render; `resources` and `database.instance.resources` — Kubernetes ResourceRequirements, read with `toYaml` and never enumerated; `rollingUpdate` — read with `with .Values.rollingUpdate`, same reason.

EXTRAS (declared though `values.yaml` omits them): `image.digest`, read by `templates/deployment.yaml` — ci-release rewrites the tag to a digest at package time (D65) and the key is absent from the shipped values; `networkPolicy.scrapeFrom.namespace`, read by `templates/networkpolicy.yaml` — `values.yaml` ships `scrapeFrom: {}`, and declaring this one key keeps `scrapeFrom` closed rather than leaving it a second open map. `tls.clientAuth`, `tls.clientCaSecret` and `tls.clientCaSecretKey`, read by `templates/deployment.yaml` only when present — the B-U5E expand (ADR-0854): `values.yaml` ships none of the three, so an adopter who never asks for client auth sees no difference, and `chart/ci/values.yaml` is REQUIRED_NO_DEFAULT's sibling list below rather than this one, because it is set rather than merely declared.

TYPES, TOGGLES AND `required` ARE RENDER CHECKS' JOB (ADR-0847), in `templates/render-checks.yaml` and `templates/scaledobject.yaml` — this file adds no `type`, `enum` or `required` to any key it did not already carry. The exceptions: `database` keeps `type: object` and `required: [migrationLockTimeoutSeconds]`, and the leaf itself keeps `type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 590` (ledger 814, ADR-0837) — the bound this file was deliberately open around before ledger 990 closed the rest of the chart. `tls.enabled` NOW carries `type: boolean` and `tls` carries `required: [enabled]` (C-DB1, ADR-0845): the binary has no compiled-in default for LISTEN_TLS_ENABLED any more, so this chart can have none for the value that renders it either. `chart/ci/values.yaml` ships `tls.enabled: true` so every shared gate that lints or renders this chart offline still has a value to coalesce (C-A2).

migrationLockTimeoutSeconds.description: Seconds a replica waits for another one's migration before failing its boot. Rendered as DB_MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and read with no fallback. Minimum 1: GET_LOCK with 0 never waits and with a negative wait never takes the lock. Maximum 590: see chart/values.yaml.
